title: 4 Visual Basic Notes
text:
COMPUTER PROGRAMMING
 A Computer program is an application used to accomplish any task imaginable in soft form.
 Basic steps in programming
 It is important to take a structured approach when programming thus implementing a program
 problem in certain order of steps.
 1. Plan the program’s tasks
 2. Design the user interface
 3. Write the program’s code
 4. Test and debug the program (using if possible alpha and beta testing methods)
 5. Document and distribute the program.
 Type of common programs
  Packaged programs they can be purchased from software stores, ordered via email and
 direct from manufacturer.
  Costumed programs they are designed for a particular or specific purpose within a given
 organization.
 STARTING VISUAL BASIC
 Create anew project, which is a set of files that store information about the components of an
 application program.
 1. Start visual basic
 2. Choose file, new project (if new project dialog box does not occur)
 3. Select or specify the type of project you want to create e.g. Standard. exe option
 4. Then click okay and you will be placed in visual basic’s design environment
 If the title bar is specified as design, it means that you are in design mode (design time) and you
 can design and code the program application.
 When the program is running and the title bar is named as run mode; this means that the program
 is running or executing.
 Visual basic applications are comprised of one or more components such as
 - Forms
 - Coded modules
 - Classes
 - Controls
 - Other components
 Visual basic has the Project explorer, which consists of a list of the contents of the current
 project. It grows as many components are added.
 RUNNING PROGRAM
 To run the program you need to execute visual basic start command using any of the methods
 - Click the start button on visual basic toolbar
 - Choose run, start
 - Press F5
 Forms
 A Form is a container that holds all the other controls such as labels, textboxes, pictures and
 access databases and make up part of the user interface.
 Control box Minimize
 button
 Caption
 Maximize button
 Closing button
 Design grid
 Forms have features found on a window in a program. It contains a title bar, a control menu, and
 asset of minimize/maximize/restore, and close buttons.
 Design time features are:
 Close buttons
 - They are always present even if the properties are set in such away that they are not
 visible at runtime.
 Design grid
 - It is a grid of dots that allows you to line up controls easily, as you are designing your
 interface.
 The form oversees the use of objects that make up the interface, including storing program codes
 that relates to the objects on the form and respond to events.
 Some form properties
 Property Name Description
 border style Sets the type of border that is used for the form
 Control box Determines whether the controlbox(containing the move and close menus)
 is visible when the program is running.
 font Determines the font used to display text on the form
 icon Determines the icon that is shown in the form’s title bar and that appears
 when the form is minimized.
 Maxbutton Determines whether the maximize button is displayed on the form when the
 program is running
 Mdichild Determines whether the form is a child form for an MDI application
 minbutton Determines whether the minimize button is displayed on the form when the
 program is running.
 startup position Determines the initial position of a form when it is first shown.
 window state Determines whether the form is shown maximized, minimized, or in its
 normal state.
 Controls
 Visual basic controls let you perform a wide variety of tasks including editing text, displaying
 pictures, and interfacing with a database. The liberal use of controls has always been one of VB
 strongest features.
 Controls are objects that perform specific tasks and have associated properties, events and
 methods.
 E.g. using a text box control, you can set properties to determine the size of the text box, the text
 that it displays and the color of the text and background.
 You are not limited to using only the control s provided by Microsoft, the design allows easy
 integration of third-party controls which increases chances of finding a control to perform almost
 any task you want, from data acquisition to custom reporting to specialized graphics processing
 to game play, and everything in between. You can create your own activex control for use in
 your programs.
 N/B
 A control is a miniature program in itself that perform certain tasks for you e.g. a
 textbox contain internal code that allows it to process keystrokes so that it knows, characters
 when you press back space key.
 Control properties
 They are adjectives that describe one specific thing about an object and modify objects
 appearance when you run your program. Hence a windows appearance is defined by a set of
 properties thus they are settings that control the appearance and behaviour of an object. All
 objects do not have it set of properties although we have common properties found in many
 objects.
 Common properties
 Name, Index, Left, Top, Height, Width, Enabled, Visible, Caption
 Left and Top
 - Describe the position of the form on the screen
 Width and height
 - Define the size of the form on the screen
 Caption
 - Dictates what is shown in an object title bar
 Name
 - Describes a unique identifier by which you can refer to the object in code.{name property
 is very important , in that it identifies the control since the program may have many
 controls of the same type and you can also use the control name property to indicate the
 procedure in which a particular code statements written.}
 Visible
 - Determines whether an object can be seen on the screen by setting it true (to be viewed)
 and false otherwise.
 Enabled
 - Determines whether the users can interact with an object setting it either to true or false.
 Control methods
 Is a program function that is built into the object. As properties, they are referenced using code
 via the dot notation
 E.g. form1.printform-prints an exact image of the form named form1on the line printer
 Although different objects have different methods, many objects have the same or common
 methods.
 Like
 Drag
 - This handles the operation of the users’ dragging and dropping the object within its
 container.
 Move
 - Changes the position of an object
 Set focus
 - Gives focus to the specified control
 Zorder
 - Determines whether an object appears in front of or behind other objects in its container.
 Controls responding to action with events
 Objects respond to actions, whether generated by the users or externally. Response to
 actions are handled through use of events .generally an object is the set of events it can
 raise and the user actions that trigger them.
 Intrinsic Controls
 CONTROL DESCRIPTION
 picture box Displays graphics .Can also serve a container for other controls.
 Label Displays text that the user
 Text box Displays text . also allows the user to enter and edit the text.
 Frame Serves as a container for other controls. Provides grouping of controls
 Command Allows the user to initiate actions by the button.
 button
 Check box Lets the user make the a true /false choice
 Option button Lets the user choose one option from a group of items.
 Box Lets the user choose form a list of items or enter anew value.
 List box Lets the user choose from a list of items.
 Horizontal Lets the user choose a scrollbar value based on the position of the
 scrollbar button in the bar.
 Vertical Serves as a horizontal scrollbar.
 scrollbar
 Timer Lets the program perform functions on timed basis.
 Drive list box Lets the user select disk drive
 Directory list Lets the user select a box directory or folder
 File list box Lets the user select a file
 Shape Displays a shape in time form
 Line Displays a line on the form
 Image Similar to a picture box control. uses fewer system resources but
 doesn’t support as many properties, events and methods..
 Data control Provides an interface between the program and a data source
 Ole Provides a connection between the program and an OLE server.
 Common Allows user of windows standard dialog boxes to retrieve information
 dialog such as file names, fonts and colors.
 Label control It does not allow the user to enter text directly; it contains events and
 properties that allow the programmer to manipulate the text directly
 from code. E.g. label caption=”time is”
 Textbox It has property that makes programs and user interaction versatile.
 Multiline and scrollbar properties in the textbox windows. They are
 useful for handling large amounts of text. Scrollbar property has affect
 on the textbox only if its multiline property is set to true
 Controls for displaying text
 Textbox and label
 Textbox
 Allow both data/text display and also allow text input. A text box control must be adding to a
 form so that it can be used.
 The textbox control is found in the tool box as one of the default controls on toolbox
 Steps followed to use a text box
 1. Click the tool for the textbox control in the toolbox. (To know if it is a text box let your
 mouse pointer pause over each control in turn to see atooltip.)
 2. Move the mouse pointer to the form .Note that the pointer will change into across hair,
 indicating that you’re about to draw the control.
 3. Move the pointer to one corner of the area where you want to draw the control.
 4. Click and hold the left mouse button
 5. Drag the mouse to where you want diagonally opposite the corner of the control.
 Label
 Are designed only to display text. They inform users what type of information is to be entered in
 the textboxes if laced next to input field. It has events and properties that allow the programmer
 to manipulate the text directly from code. If you want to display more text, pay attention to the
 auto size and word wrap properties. If auto size is true the size of the label control automatically
 adjusts to fit the text being displayed, otherwise label remains same size.
 If word wrap is false the label expands horizontally to a low the caption to fit, even if the label
 grows so large that it passes the right edge of the screen. If the word wrap is true the label
 expands vertically to allow enough times of text to accommodate the caption even if the label
 runs off the bottom edge of the screen.
 Steps followed to use a label
 1. Select the label control’s tool in the tool box
 2. Draw a label control to the left of the first text box control
 3. In the properties window change the label control’s name property to start with lbl e.g.
 lblbookid
 4. Change the label control’s caption property to <name>
 i. lblbookid.caption=<name>
 5. change the label’s alignment property to suit your application
 e.g. lblbookid.alignment = 0-leftjustify
 1-rightjustify
 2-center
 The command button
 This control lets users initiate actions by clicking the button. you can set up a command button
 control by
 o Drawing the button on the form
 o Then set the caption property to the text that you want displayed on the button’s
 face.
 o To activate the button, just place code in the button’s click event procedure.
 To access commands through the keyboard
 You make use of access keys assigned using the ampersand sign “&” ,on the button caption.
 To use the access key, the user holds down the alt key and processes the access key to trigger the
 command button controls’ a click event.
 e.g. command1.caption=&”print”
 It will appear as Print and to use the command using the keyboard press alt + p
 Checkboxes
 when a checkbox is on ,a check mark() is d displayed in the box.It indicates that the answer to
 the checkbox ‘s corresponding question is “yes’ .when the checkbox is off or unchecked the
 box is empty, indicates an answer of “NO”
 option buttons-they exist a group and only one of them can be selected at a time .They are useful
 for presenting a fixed list of mutually exclusive choices.
 Two ways of using the option button.
 1.) Use the click event if you want to take an action when users select an option. This is useful
 when using control array and code is typed in the option procedure.
 2.) Do not write any code in the optional button event .Instead use if statement in a relevant
 controls procedure e.g. button to check if they are true .
 The list box
 -The key parts of the list box are the following
 Item list
 o Which is the list of items from which the users can select.
 o They are added to the list in the design environment or by our program as it is
 running mostly using code
 Select item
 This item is chosen by the users. Depending on the style of list you choose a
 selected item indicated by a highlight bar or by a check in the box next to the
 item.
 Scroll bar
 This part indicates that more items are available on the list than will fit in the box
 and provides the users with an easy way to view the addition items. , But it does
 not have horizontal scrollbar although vertical scrollbar appear as default.
 Filling list box using code
 Private sub form_load()
 Dim I as integer
 For I=1 to 100
 List1.AddItem I
 Next I
 To clear using clear method
 List1.clear
 To print items from the list you can use list property of the list box indexed from “ 0”
 Print list1.list (index)
 Listcount-represent the number of items in alistbox
 List1.listcount
 Listindex- represent index of selected items.
 List1.ListIndex
 Removeitem-remove item from the item list by specifying the array index of the item.this
 property works only for asingle selection.
 List1.RemoveItem ListIndex
 Using index with additem method you can specify the location within the list where you want
 the new item to appear.
 Setting the appearance of a list box
 This can be done by using or setting the style property to either:
 0-standard
 1-checkbox
 the values can be changed at runtime by setting its value to one of the intrinsic
 constants
 vblistboxstandard or vblistboxcheckbox respectively
 the otherway to change the list’s APPEARANCE is to use the columns property that has
 a default value of zero
 Setting it to 1
 Causes the list to be presented with one column at atime,but to scroll horizontally
 instead of vertically.
 Setting it to values greater than 1
 Causes the list to display in ,the number of columns specified by the property.
 Working with multiple selections
 Applicable only when you need to select more than one element .this is done using multiselect
 property and it has three possible setting.
 1. 0-none
 Is default setting showing that multiple selection is not required or permitted.
 2. 1-simple
 Users can click an item with the mouse to select it or click a selected item to
 deselect it. Using the keyboard, users can make use of the cursor keys to move the
 focus (dotted line border)to an item and then presss the space bar to select or
 deselect it.
 3. 2-extended
 Is more complex, here users can use standard windows techniques to quickly
 select multiple items.you can select a range of items by clicking the first item in
 the range and then ,while holding down the shift key,click the last item in the
 range; all items in between the first and lat items are selected .to add or delete a
 single item to or from the selection,userts hold down the control key while
 clicking the item.
 Selected property is an array that has an element for each item in the list. The value of the
 selected property for each item is either true (if the item is selected) or false (when not selected).
 To display item selected you can print on the form
 e.g.
 numitem=list1.listcount
 For I=0 to numitem-1
 If list1.selected (I) then
 Form1.print list1.list (I)
 End if
 Next I
 The combo box
 - The use of combo boxes can be done in three different ways.
 1.) The drop-down combo box
 Presents the users with a text box combined with a drop down list. The users can either
 select an item from the list portion or type an item in the text box portion
 2.) The simple combo box
 Displays a textbox and a list that doesn’t drop down.
 3.) The drop down list
 Displays drops down list box from which the users can make achoice. The users cannot
 enter items that not in the list. As a list box it uses AddItem, RemoveItem, and clear
 methods to modify the contents of the list, but combo box mainly lacks support for
 multiple selections, although it allows you to enter choices
 Filling combo box using code
 Private sub form_load ()
 Dim I as integer
 For I=1 to 100
 Combo1.AddItem I
 Next I
 To clear using clear method
 combo1.clear
 To print items from the combo list you can use list property of the combo box that is
 indexed from “ 0”
 Print combo1.list (index)
 Special _purpose controls
  Scrollbar control
  Timer control
  Frame control
 SCROLLBAR CONTROL
 Provides agraphical way for you to perform tasks such as control your position within
 adocument or make adjustments.visual basic has two types of scrollbars for entering
 numerical data
 The vertical scrollbar –vScrollBar
 The horizontal scrollbar –HscrollBar
 Setting up the scrollbar
 To use ascrollbar, you simply use appropriate properties to set and retrieve the
 range and values. The three most important properties used with scroll bar s both
 at design time and runtime.
 Value-retrieves or sets the current numeric value
 Min-controls the minimum value of the value property
 Max –controls the maximum value of the value property
 THE TIMER CONTROL
 The timer usually execute code when the interval is complete.The timer control counts down
 repeatedly ,as long as the enabled property is set to true.The timer control is designed to work
 with very small amounts of time ;the maximum setting is just alittle longer than a minute.
 The timer control is used for scheduling and performing repeated operation.
 To Setting up timer
 Draw it on the form
 Always shows up as an icon at design time, but it does not show up at all while your program is
 running.
 Place the code for events generation in the timer event and then
 To make use of timer
 Set the interval property
 It is set to zero by default disabling the timer control. This property can be set to any
 value between zero to 65535,with the amount of time in milliseconds.
 Set the enabled property to true
 It acts like aswitch that turns your timer on and off.If the timer control is ena bled,the
 code in the timer event is executed at the end of the time specified in the interval
 property.
 THE FRAME CONTROL
 Is aspecial type of control called a container.Containers are controls in which you can draw other
 controls,much like areal picture frame visually encloses(or contains) an artist’s picture.At this
 point ,you can set several properties that control the apprearance of the frame.
 e.g.
 caption-the text that is entered in the caption property will appear in the upper_left corner of the
 frame .Is used to identify the contents of the frame or provide other descriptive information.
 Appearance-dectates whether the border is shown as a single –line ,single color border,which
 gives the control aflat look ,or a 3D effect.
 Borderstyle-this property determines whether the border around the frame is displayed.
 MENUS
 Menu system can be created using the menu editor. You can use this editor to create a menu bar
 for each of your application’s form as well as context –sensitive “pop-up menus {menu system
 enable a program user to locate and execute its functions easily}
 To create menu, first open the form on which you want the menu located, and then start the menu
 editor in any of the three ways
 Click the menu editor button on the tool bar
 ♣ Choose tools, menu editor
 ♣ Press
 ♣ Control +E
 You use the ampersand sign next to the menu caption first character, which is to become the
 access key.
 Access keys offer users away to navigate amenu system by using the keyboard instead of a
 menu. If a menu item has an access key defined, it is indicated by an underscore beneath the
 letter in the item’s caption.
 Shortcut keys provide direct access to a function through a single key (such as delete) or key
 combination (such as control+s), bypassing the menu system entirely.
 To assign a short cut key
 1.) Enter the menu editor, select the menu item for which you want ashorrt cut key.
 2.) Then select the desired key from the short cut list.
 The key is assigned to that function, and the short cut key information appears next to the menu
 item in the menu.
 Generally assigning shortcut key
  Select form and then open the menu editor
  Click the print menu item to select it
  Click the drop down arrow next to the short cut list and select control + p from the
 list
  Click ok to close
 WRITING CODE
 Visual basic is an object oriented, event driven language. The user initiates events, by writing
 code that respond to those events appropriately, in the object event procedure. Procedure or sub
 procedure is a discrete sequence of code statements that has a name and is executed as a unit.
 You can double click
 To get code view
 You can double_click the controls to get the control event procedure
 Click code view icon in the project explorer
 Highlight menu view then in the drop down menu highlight code view
 Then type code
 e.g . In exit procedure control
 Private sub cmdexit _click ()
 End
 End sub
 Sub procedure
 To indent the code you press tab: Indenting code makes it easier to read and trace the code
 A comment is a line that explains what’s going on, a comment is denoted by a single quotation
 mark (‘), usually at the beginning of a line. When the visual basic interpreter encounters a single
 quote on a line, the remainder of the line is ignored. Visual basic moves to interpret the next line
 for next instruction.
 Visual basic continuation character ( _ ) will be used at the end of the line that is broken.
 Although you can leave this character out and type the code in a single line.
 Keyboard hotkeys are indicated with underlining .you use ALT + <CHARACTER TOBE
 UNDERLINED> to select the menu item
 In the code view /window we have two drop down list boxes at the top
 The object box (one on the left) lists all the objects that have been placed on the current
 form, as well as the form itself.
 The procedure box (on the right) lists all the events that apply to whichever object that is
 currently selected in the object box.
 Writing program code
 Initialize or declare variables
 A variable is a temporary storage location for information or unique identifier of a given type.
 Declaration
 The first part of the program/procedures is used to declare the variables you’ll need .telling visual
 basic the variables that the procedure will be using ,as well as what type of information each
 variable may contain.
 Procedure code is part of code remaining in the procedure that do not work.
 Declaration of variables
 Visual basic supports two types of declaring variables.
 Explicit
 Implicit
 Explicit
 In this type of declaration you make use of statements to define the names and dta types of your
 program’s variables. The statements do not assign values to the variables but merely tell visual
 basic what the variables should be called and what data they can contain.
 e.g.
 Dim varname [as vartype]
 Private Varname [as vartype]
 Public varname [as vartype]
 Static varname [as varitype]
 Implicit
 You can assign a type as in the declaration above but in this type of declaration a special
 character is used at the end of the variable name when the variable is first assigned a value.
 DATA TYPE CHARACTER
 Integer %
 Long &
 single !
 double #
 currency @
 string $
 The above data types are the only type that have special characters the rest have none.
 e.g.
 explicit nNumVal=0 sStr=”my name” fNum=10.1
 implicit nNumVal%=0 sStr$=”my name” fNum! =10.1
 Fixed length strings
 Most string types that are used in visual basic are of variable length. They contain any amount of
 text up to 2 billion characters and can be declared in both implicit and explicit declaration.
 Dynamic string variables usually adjust automatically in size to accommodate the length of the
 string.
 In fixed length strings ,string variable size remain the same ,regardless of the text assignment.so
 the expression assigned to the variable should be shorter than the defined length of the variables
 , and the remaining length of the variable is field with spaces.if the expression is longer only the
 assigned length that fit the length will be stored while the rest of text will be trancated.fixed
 length string variables can only be declared using an explicit declaration.
 Variable arrays
 Arrays are normally declared as
 <Varname> (size) as [vartype]
 e.g. Dim nData (1 to 20) as integer
 But variable array declaration will be declared as
 <Varname> () as [vartype]
 e.g. Dim nData () as integer
 sname=”people”
 Redim nData (1 to len (sname))
 Public variables are global thus they can be accessed anywhere in the program
 Dim/private variables are localized variables hence they are used within the scope of the
 procedure or form. Thus they are known as form level or module _level
 variables
 Static variables retain the current value of variables within a running procedure. Normally
 variables are discarded by visual basic when the procedure is finished, but when you need to call
 the procedure several times you need to preserve the value of a variable even after the procedure
 is run and the variable for one call to the procedure is dependent on the value left over from
 previous calls
 e.g. static npagenumber as integer
 Constant variables are declared at the beginning of the form program or procedure and they
 constant variable store the value permanently and they can be used within the level of declaration
 without changing in value.
 Const <varname>=value
 e.g. Public const pie=3.142
 TYPES PREFIX RANGE MEMORY
 REQ
 Integers n -31768 to 32767 2 bytes Whole numbers
 Long l Approximately +/- 2 4 bytes
 billion
 Byte B 0-255 1 byte
 Single f +/-(1E-45 to 3E38) 8 byte Decimal numbers
 (float)
 Double d +/-(5E-324 to 1.8E308) 8 byte
 Currency c +/-9E14 8 byte Numbers with up to 15
 digits left of the decimal
 and four digits right of the
 decimal
 String s 65400char for fixed length 1 byte per Text information
 string and 2 billion for character
 dynamic string
 Date D 1/1/100 to 31/12/9999 8 byte Date and time information
 Boolean b True/false 2 byte Logical values
 Object o Instances of class; ole 4 byte
 objects
 Variant v Accepts any of the above 16 bytes
 or preceding data types
 Visual basic program constructs
 Sequences
 Visual basic program allows the programmer to place the code in agiven set or order of
 execution.
 Example
 Print “ hallo world”
 Print “ we want peace”
 Selection
 It uses section constructs to make choices
 Example
 If then
 Syntax
 If <condition> then
 (statement)
 end if
 example
 if (Not adodc1.recordset.eof)=true then
 print adodc1.recordset.fields(0).value
 adodc1.recordset.movenext
 end if
 if then else
 syntax
 if <condition> then
 statement (if condition is true)
 else
 statement (if condition is false)
 end if
 example
 if k<=100 then
 print “ iam within the limit”
 else
 print “iam over board”
 end if
 Nesting If Statement
 Method 1
 if <condition1> then
 if <condition2> then
 statement1
 end if
 statement 2
 else
 if <condition3> then
 statement3
 else
 statement 4
 end if
 end if
 Method2
 if <conditon1> then
 statement1
 elseif<condition2>then
 statement2
 elseif<condition3> then
 statement3
 end if
 ITERATIONS
 Loops continuously in accordance with the loop condition statement status
 Do while
 Syntax
 Do while <condition>
 Statement
 Loop
 Example
 Do while I<20
 List1.Additem I
 I=I+1
 Loop
 Do until
 Syntax
 Do until<condition>
 Statement
 Loop
 Example
 Do until j>19
 Combo1.additem j
 J=j+1
 Loop
 Do loop while
 Syntax
 Statement
 Loop while<condition>
 Example
 Print “new number” & k
 K=k+1
 Loop while k<100
 For to do
 Syntax
 For varname=initialvalue to maxvalue
 Statement
 Next varname
 Example
 For l=0 to 20
 T(l)=0
 Next l
 While do
 Syntax
 While <condition>
 Statement
 Wend
 Example
 While rsmine.eof=false
 Print rsmine.fields(0).value
 Wend
 The with statement
 Syntax
 With statement
 statement
 End with
 Example
 With adodc1.recordset
 !delete(adaffectcurrent)
 end with
 Math operators
 OPERATION SIGN
 Addition +
 Subtraction -
 Multiplication *
 Division /
 Integer division \
 Modulus Mod
 Exponentiation ^
 String functions
 Visual basic supports only one string operator the combination or concatenation Operator that is
 the ampersand sign (&). It joins two string or a string and a value
 syntax
 new string=string1 & string 2
 example
 sk =”my name” & “ is my country”
 Visual basic string function
 Lcase
 It converts all text to lower case
 Syntax
 Lcase (string)
 Example
 Lcase (“KENYA MY COUNTRY”)
 ‘Returns “Kenya my country”
 Ucase
 It converts all text to upper case
 Syntax
 Ucase (string)
 Example
 Ucase (“hallo Kenya”)
 ‘Returns ‘HALLO KENYA”
 Instr/InstrRev
 Returns the location value of a search string inside another string
 Instr
 Syntax
 Instr (startingpt, sourcestr, searchstr, casemode)
 0----case sensitive
 1----non case sensitive
 vbbinarycompare
 Example
 Instr(1,”together”,”e”,vbtextcompare)
 ‘returns 4
 InstrRev
 Syntax
 InstrRev(sourcestr,searchstr,startingpt,casemode)
 Example
 InstrRev(“Example”,”a”,-1,1)
 ‘returns 3
 Len
 Returns the size or length of the string
 Syntax
 Len(string)
 Example
 Len(“mypeople”)
 ,returns 8
 Trim
 Removes spaces from the whole string
 Syntax
 Trim(string)
 Example
 Sp=” my country my people “
 Trim (sp)
 ‘returns “my country my people”
 Rtrim
 Removes spaces from the right side of the string
 Syntax
 Rtrim(string)
 Example
 Rtrim(sp)
 ‘returns “ my country my people”
 Ltrim
 Removes spaces from the left part of the string
 Syntax
 Ltrim(string)
 Example
 Ltrim(sp)
 ‘returns “my country my people “
 Left
 Retrieves a specific amount of characters from the left part of the string
 Syntax
 Left (string,numchar)
 Example
 Left(“application”,3)
 ‘returns “app”
 Right
 Retrieve or specifies a specific number of characters from the right part of the string
 Syntax
 Right(string,numchar)
 Example
 Right(“application”,3)
 ‘returns “ion”
 Mid
 Retrieves or replaces the specified amount of text in a string
 Syntax
 mid(sourcestr,[startingpt,numchar)
 Retrieves
 Svalue=mid$(“today”,2,3)
 ‘ returns “oda”
 replaces
 mid$(“today”,2,3)=”XXX”
 ‘returns “txxxy”
 StrReverse
 reverses the order of characters in a string
 syntax
 strReverse(string)
 example
 strReverse(“yelling”)
 ‘Returns “gnilley”
 Chr
 converts ASCII numbers(0 to 255) to related ASCII letter,alphanumeric,and numbers
 syntax
 chr(value)
 example
 chr(65)
 ‘returns “A”
 Asc
 The inverse of Chr() converts ASCII letters,alphanumerics and numbers into number values.
 Syntax
 Asc(string)
 Example
 Asc(“a”)
 ‘returns 97
 asc(“”)
 ‘returns 32
 CStr/Str
 Convert values or variables value into strings

 Procedures and functions
 Procedures
 They are subroutines or segments of code that perform a particular task and then return
 processing to the area of the code from which they where called .
 Advantages
 - You can test each task individually (the smaller am,ount of code enable or make
 debugging easier)
 - Help eliminate redundant code by calling procedure instead of repeating program code
 every time.
 - You can create a library of procedures to be used in more than one program
 - Makes program maintenance easier.

 RECORDSET
 They are three types of record sets supported by visual basic
 1. Tables
 2. Dynaset
 3. Snapshot
 TABLE
 A table (table type recordset) is a directly link to one of the physical tables stored in the database.
 this type of recordset provides the most direct link to the data. They are the only form of record
 sets that support indexes; hence searching a table for a specific record can be quicker than
 searching a dynaset or snapshot. when using tables data is addressed or modified from one table
 at a time, one record at a time
 Advantages of using tables
 You can use or create indexes to change the presentation order of the data in the tables during
 program execution.
 You can perform rapid searches for an individual record using appropriate index and the seek
 command
 Changes made to the tables by other concurrent users or programs are immediately available.
 Disadvantages
 You can’t set filters on a table to limit the records being processed to a certain criteria.
 You can’t use find commands on a table(seek command finds only the first record that meets its
 criteria .
 Using ADODC
 Adodc1.CommandType = adCmdTable
 Adodc1.RecordSource = "STUDENT"
 Adodc1.Refresh
 Using OLEDB CONNECTION
 Set rctest = New ADODB.Recordset
 rctest.Open "student", DCTEST, adOpenStatic, adLockOptimistic
 Using DAO
 Set rsmine = dbmine.OpenRecordset("STUDENT", dbOpenTable)
 DYNASET
 Is a group of information from one or more tables in a database .this information is composed of
 selected fields from the tables. Often presented in a specific order and filtered by a specific
 condition. they are updateable record sets and address the records present in the base tables at the
 time they are created. Although they do not automatically reflect additions or deletions of records
 made by users or programs after the dynaset is created. Dynaset is actually asset of record
 pointers that point to the specified data as it existed when the dynaset is created. {A dynaset is
 actually a set of record pointers that point to a specified data as it existed when the dynaset was
 created).
 Dynaset support information changes such as addition, edits and deletions.
 Advantages of using dynasets
 Dynasets enable you to join information from multiple tables
 You can use find methods to locate or process every record meeting a specified criteria.
 They enable limiting of the number of fields or records so are retrieved into the recordset.
 They make use of filters and sort order properties to change the view of data.
 You can’t use indexes with dynaset hence you can’t change the presentation order of the dynaset
 by changing the index or by creating anew one.
 It does not automatically reflect additions or deletions

 Adodc1.CommandType = adCmdText
 Adodc1.RecordSource = "SELECT * FROM STUDENT"
 Adodc1.Refresh

 Set rsmine = dbmine.OpenRecordset("SELECT * FROM STUDENT",
 dbOpenDynaset)
 SNAPSHOTS
 As the name implies,it is a “picture”, or copy ,of the data in a recordset at a particular point in
 time .They are similar to a dynaset in that it is created from base tables, using sql statements or
 from aquerydefinition,dynaset or another snapshots. the difference of dynaset to a snapshot
 whenever you want a set of data that isn’t time sensitive.(it does not matter if the records are
 updated after creation of the snapshot.
 Advantages
 You can join information from multiple tables
 You can use the find method
 Record navigation and record set creation can be faster
 Disadvantage
 They are not updatable or indexes

 DATA CONTROL
 Is a link between information in your database and the bound controls that you use to display the
 information.to use a data control you must
 1.) set the database to connect to from the properties
 2.) Select the part of the database to access.
 By default the data control creates a dynaset_type recordset from one or more of the tables in
 your database.
 Steps to follow when setting up a data control
 1.) select the data control on your form
 2.) draw the control on your form
 3.) set the databasename property control
 4.) set the recordsource property control
 using code
 data1.databasename=app. path & “\students.mbd”
 =<data base name with full path>
 data1.recordsource= “select * from <tablename>”;
 Data control is quick and easy but it lacks a few capabilities that are necessary for must data
 entry applications specifically adding and deleting records.
 1.) adding records_
 data1.recordset.addnew
 it allows one to enter new record,after ablank re3cord is prepared in the copy
 buffer,which is a special place where records are edited before actually being entered into
 the database(you edit a new record).
 2.) edit mode_allows you to change the information in record.
 3.) update_ commits the data in the copy buffer to the database when method is evoked.
 DATA ACCESS OBJECTS (DAO)
 is amore complex data use method where program commands are used and acts as an internal
 representation of physical data, data stored in some type of database or data management engine.
 the key reason for using program commands is the flexibility they give you beyond what is
 available with the data control. It allows you to perform more detailed input validation that is
 possible with built-in database engine rules because program commands do not directly access
 the database.

 to create a database object in your program,.

 entire table,specific fields and records from the table,or acombination of records and fields from
 multiple tables.

 1.) Create reports using PRINT REPORTING FUNCTION and other
 graphics methods. (Use of third party reporting addin)
 o It is time wastage and also wastes effort

 2.) USING THE DATA REPORT
 Enable display of a print preview screen, with print and export buttons, from an ADO data
 source.
 It is also known as an activex designer
 The report has five main sections
 Report header - information is displayed only once at the top of the report.
 Page header - information is displayed at the top of every page.
 Detail section -This section or part of the report is repeated for every or each record in
 the ADO data source.
 Page footer -Information displayed at the button of every page
 Report footer -Information displayed at the end of report.
 Data report controls
 Rpt label -specifies a label used to display text that is not data bound, such as a
 column name or date printed.
 Rpt textbox - displays the contents of a database field. (Only used in the detail
 section).
 Rpt image - contains a picture or other graphic image, such as accompany logo.
 Rpt line -Enables you to draw lines on the report _for example to separate the
 different sections of the report
 Rpt shape -Enables you to draw a variety of shapes on the control to highlight
 information or provide other visual effects.
 Rpt function -Allows you to place a field in the header or footer that contains one of
 several simple math functions, such as a total of all the other values
 in a particular data field.

 Private Function flsh(sign As String, num As Double, otext As Object)
 If sign = "+" Then
 flsh = num + Val(otext.Text)
 ElseIf sign = "-" Then
 If num <> 0 Then
